subject: Portability evaluation & success hypothesis — post-call recap
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0500
Subject: Portability evaluation & success hypothesis — post-call recap

Anita / team — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and concrete next steps so we’re aligned. I captured what we heard on the call plus our proposed success hypothesis for a portability evaluation.

Key pain points you raised
- Token costs on current OpenAI + Anthropic mix are creating monthly variability and pushing up per-session spend.
- Hard rate-limit behaviour during peak batch jobs (billing/alerts spike when ingesting nightly transcripts).
- Residency & audit requirements for PHI-like metadata; procurement wants proof of KMS/HSM + audit logs.
- Embeddings drift: search relevance drops when models change upstream.

Current stack (as stated)
- Frontend -> internal API gateway -> enrichment layer -> OpenAI (chat/completions) and Anthropic (assistant)
- Local Redis cache for short-lived context; no persistent KV cache across sessions today
- PostgreSQL for metadata and user profiles; all PII in a separate encrypted DB

Success hypothesis (what a successful migration/portability proof looks like)
- Latency: end-to-end p95 < 200ms for standard assist flows (50 token generation + context lookup).
- Cost: 35–50% reduction in per-conversation inference spend versus current blended baseline.
- Quality: parity on the 10-15 canonical prompts you provided (>=95% acceptance by your QA reviewers).
- Security/compliance: ability to deploy under your VPC and integrate with your KMS + audit logs for sensitive calls.

Compatibility needs we flagged
- Function/tool calling parity (you rely on structured JSON outputs for orchestration).
- Streaming support for partial-response UX.
- Tokenization/embeddings compatibility or migration mapping (ability to reindex or translate embeddings).
- Stable model variants for deterministic embedding behavior.

Preliminary model shortlist (subject to tech-deep-dive)
- Redwood-verified Llama2-70b quantized variant (candidate for most workloads)
- MPT / Mosaic ML medium-large family (cost-efficient option)
- 8–16B dense open-weights model for low-latency endpoints
- Fallback: smaller Anthropic-compatible flavor for assistant parity (to reduce feature risk)

Proposed next steps and owners
1) Technical deep-dive (Priyom to lead) — 60–90m session: mapping current API calls, embeddings pipeline, and function-calling examples. Please confirm availability next week (we suggested Wed or Thu).
2) PoC: we’ll provision a secure, temporary test workspace with sample anonymized transcripts (HealthScale to provide) and run a 2-week portability trial. (Ben / Logan to coordinate access + SSO/KMS notes).
3) Cost model & one-pager: Redwood will produce a TCO sketch (tokens, infra, ops) and an estimated run-rate delta for a 6-month horizon.
4) Security evidence: share SOC2 + data residency playbook; HealthScale security team to confirm any additional evidence needed.

Attachments: portability-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet with checklist + prompt set); call-recording-20261114.mp3 (recording).
Related links: HubSpot deal HS-2026-0421 (https://app.hubspot.com/deals/HS-2026-0421); shared PoC folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C4dHealthScale-PoC).

Open items / decisions needed from HealthScale
- Which three canonical prompts should be in scope for the PoC?
- Procurement: high-level timeline for a signed SOW (approx ballpark)?
- Security: can you share a small sample of the metadata schema we should expect to ingest (anonymized)?

If that aligns, we’ll lock the deep-dive slot and Priyom will send a calendar invite with an agenda and requested artifacts.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this along.

—

- Embeddings: preserving semantic parity is critical; if we can’t get deterministic migration we’ll need a reindex plan.

For next steps — Wed 2026-11-18 or Thu 2026-11-19 for the technical deep-dive would work for us (prefer mornings PT). Please send an invite with the agenda and the specific API call samples you want.

Also: can you include a short one-pager that maps the current OpenAI/Anthropic calls to the proposed compatibility layer and a ballpark cost delta (high/medium/low scenarios)? That will help the director review.

Thanks — Anita
